text:
maria: heads up — noticing ~30% throughput drop on dedicated pool dc-prod-rtpool-3 starting ~02:10 UTC. p95 spiked from 90ms -> 220ms, occasional 429s. graphs: https://grafana/redwood/d/rtpool/dc-prod-rtpool-3

ops-bot: [alert] autoscaler/throttle spike on dc-prod-rtpool-3 at 2026-03-17T02:11:08Z — see incident link

raj: oncall looking. any deploys or config rollouts around 02:00?

maria: no code deploys. config rollout: scheduler quantum was bumped to 64 in canary at 02:00 by rollout job (notes attached).

sam: I see queue-depth oscillation in the same time window. small microbatches and a lot of prefill churn. suspect quantum vs continuous-batcher mismatch — prefill starvation.

elaine: can you collect a per-GPU batch-size histogram and prefill log for a hot shard? command:
```
kubectl -n runtime exec -it batcher-hotpod -- /bin/sh -c 'curl -s localhost:9100/metrics | grep batch_size_histogram'
```

maria: pasted the histogram from one hot GPU — distribution heavily skewed to batch_size=1-4, almost nothing near target 32/64.
```
batch_size_bucket{le="1"} 4821
batch_size_bucket{le="4"} 12003
batch_size_bucket{le="16"} 12210
...
```

raj: that looks like prefill is failing because the scheduler quantum (64) causes the scheduler to prefer filling up slots with small-token requests rather than aggregating. combined with low max_batch_tokens, we end up with many tiny microbatches.

sam: also noticed autoscaler reacted to pending queue growth and attempted scale-out, but pool is at reserved capacity (8/8) and burst is disabled -> throttle/429s for tenants. billing/quota didn't change. ops-bot shows reserved_capacity_used=8.

elaine: short-term mitigation options:
- roll scheduler quantum back to 32
- bump max_batch_tokens to 4096 for the pool so token-limited prefill can aggregate better
- temporarily re-route heavy tenants to dc-prod-rtpool-4 if available

maria: applying config change now:
```
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: runtime.redwood/v1
kind: PoolConfig
metadata:
  name: dc-prod-rtpool-3
spec:
  schedulerQuantum: 32
  maxBatchTokens: 4096
EOF
```

maria: kubectl apply OK. will watch metrics.

(2m later) maria: batch_size histogram shifting — more mass around 16-32, average batch tokens up ~2.5x. throughput +20% and p95 trending down. errors 429 dropped. :relieved:

raj: good. we'll keep this mitigation for 24h while we investigate root cause. file a follow-up.

elaine: root cause hypothesis: the scheduler quantum change increased the scheduler's ticket size so continuous batcher got fragmented across many small token requests (quantum too large relative to request token distribution). the scheduler needs a heuristic to adapt quantum against observed token-length histogram and max_batch_tokens.

sam: action items:
- elaine: RFC + Jira for adaptive-quantum heuristic + unit/regression tests (assign to elaine)
- raj: update runbook to include quick checks (batch histogram, reserved_capacity_used, scheduler quantum rollback steps)
- maria: monitor for 24h and post if regressions reappear

elaine: creating JIRA RED-1248 "adaptive scheduler quantum + safety checks" and drafting RFC. will include a perf harness to simulate token distributions.

maria: thanks all. leaving thread open for follow-up. :thumbsup:
